'''Ira N. Levine''' (February 12, 1937 – December 17, 2015) was an American author, scientist,  professor and faculty member in the chemistry department at [[Brooklyn College]]. He is widely acknowledged for his research in the field of [[microwave spectroscopy]], and for several widely known textbooks in [[physical chemistry]] and [[quantum chemistry]]. 

== Biography ==
Levine was born in [[Brooklyn]], New York. He was graduated from [[Erasmus Hall High School]]. In 1952, Levine was graduated with an honorary degree in chemistry and named as top scholastic honorary graduate in the College of Engineering and Science at [[Carnegie Mellon College of Engineering]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=1958-07-11|title=Pittsburgh sun-telegraph. Five Honorary Degree Awarded, 793 Graduate From Carnegie Institute of Tech.|language=English|page=9|work=Pittsburgh sun-telegraph.|issue=Second Ed. June 11, 1958|oclc=2266192}}</ref> In 1959, he went on to graduate school in the field of [[physical chemistry]] and [[mathematical physics]] at Harvard University.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Jaques Cattell Press|title=American men & women of science: physical and biological sciences|date=1986|publisher=Bowker|location=New York|pages=723|language=English|oclc=13680380}}</ref> In 1963, he was awarded a PhD in chemistry under the guidance of Professor [[Edgar Bright Wilson|E. Bright Wilson]] by [[Harvard University]].<ref name="levinephd">{{Cite thesis|title=The microwave spectrum and structure of formaldoxime.|date=1963|language=English|first=Ira Noel|last=Levine|degree=PhD|publisher=Harvard University|oclc=1035321801}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Levine|first=Ira|title=Chemistry @Brooklyn College Ingersoll Hall (Physical & Theoretical Chemistry)|url=http://academic.brooklyn.cuny.edu/chem/NEW-WEB/facultyindex/PhysicalBC.htm|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718185849/http://academic.brooklyn.cuny.edu/chem/NEW-WEB/facultyindex/PhysicalBC.htm|archive-date=2021-07-18|access-date=2021-07-18|website=academic.brooklyn.cuny.edu}}</ref><ref name="levinephdthesis">{{Cite journal|last=|date=November 1963|title=Dissertation abstracts|journal=Dissertation Abstracts|language=English|publisher=University Microfilms|volume=24|page=1850|issn=0099-3123|oclc=3612889}}</ref> He started his academic career at Brooklyn College in 1964 where he taught first-year courses in general chemistry as well as advanced courses in physical and quantum chemistry. He became a full-time professor in 1978. Levine is recognized for several textbooks he authored and for his research in physical chemistry, quantum chemistry and microwave spectroscopy. Levine textbooks include Quantum Chemistry (7th ed.),<ref>{{Cite book|last=Levine|first=Ira N|title=Quantum chemistry|date=2019|publisher=Pearson |isbn=978-93-325-5853-3|language=English|oclc=1224329858}}</ref> Physical Chemistry (6th ed.),<ref>{{Cite book|last=Levine|first=Ira N|title=Physical chemistry|date=2017|publisher=McGraw-Hill|isbn=978-1-308-97449-1|location=Boston|language=English|oclc=1113176995}}</ref> Solutions Manual to Physical Chemistry (5th ed.),<ref>{{Cite book|last=Levine|first=Ira N|title=Student solutions manual to accompany Physical chemistry, fifth edition|date=2002|publisher=McGraw-Hill|isbn=978-0-07-239360-6|location=Boston; London|language=English|oclc=990718317}}</ref> and a textbook on Molecular Spectroscopy.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Levine|first=Ira N|title=Molecular spectroscopy|date=1975|publisher=Wiley|isbn=978-0-471-53128-9|location=New York|language=English|oclc=1121066}}</ref> His textbooks have been translated into many languages, including Arabic, Chinese, Czech, Hungarian, Polish, Spanish and Portuguese and they have been used by many Chemistry departments in the US and elsewhere. He died on December 17, 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-07-18|title=IRA LEVINE Obituary (2015) - New York, NY - New York Times|website=[[Legacy.com]]|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/nytimes/name/ira-levine-obituary?pid=176961140|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718161552/https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/nytimes/name/ira-levine-obituary?pid=176961140|archive-date=2021-07-18|access-date=2021-07-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-07-18|title=A Farewell Letter to Professor Levine – The Macaulay Messenger|url=https://eportfolios.macaulay.cuny.edu/messenger/2015/12/29/a-farewell-letter-to-professor-levine/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718144821/https://eportfolios.macaulay.cuny.edu/messenger/2015/12/29/a-farewell-letter-to-professor-levine/|archive-date=2021-07-18|access-date=2021-07-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-07-18|title=IRA LEVINE Obituary - North Lauderdale, FL|url=https://www.dignitymemorial.com/en-ca/obituaries/north-lauderdale-fl/ira-levine-9838989|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718173920/https://www.dignitymemorial.com/en-ca/obituaries/north-lauderdale-fl/ira-levine-9838989|archive-date=2021-07-18|access-date=2021-07-18}}</ref>
